name: ADS1118 16-bit SPI ADC with temperature sensor
description: Texas Instruments 16-bit delta-sigma ADC with 4 single-ended / 2 differential inputs, programmable gain (+/-0.256 to +/-6.144 V full scale), 8-860 samples/s, internal reference and a built-in temperature sensor (0.03125 degC/LSB), read over SPI (mode 1). Runs on 2-5.5 V. Sold as: ADS1118 16-bit ADC Breakout Board (PMD Way, red 17 x 16 mm board marked HW-420), two 6-pin headers: GND, VIN, SCK, CS, OUT, DIN and GND, VIN, A0, A1, A2, A3.
eli5: Measures up to four voltages very precisely (much finer than the ESP32's own ADC) and also tells you its own temperature.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply to the chip's VDD, 2-5.5 V. Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico: OUT swings to VIN

pins.name: SCK
pins.description: SPI clock (SCLK), up to 4 MHz, SPI mode 1

pins.name: OUT
pins.description: DOUT/DRDY: conversion data out; also goes low (with CS low) when a new result is ready

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: Data in: the 16-bit Config word, latched on SCLK falling edges

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Ground (printed GND on the analog header, same net as GND)

pins.name: VIN2
pins.description: Supply (printed VIN on the analog header, same net as VIN)

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Analog input AIN0, GND to VIN (never above VIN + 0.3 V or below GND - 0.3 V)

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Analog input AIN1, GND to VIN

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Analog input AIN2, GND to VIN

pins.name: A3
pins.description: Analog input AIN3, GND to VIN

buildNotes: SPI mode 1 (polarity=0, phase=1), at most 4 MHz. Mode 0 shifts every bit and gives garbage.

Each 16-bit transfer writes the Config register on DIN while the PREVIOUS conversion result comes out on OUT. Single-shot: write config with SS=1, wait 1/data-rate (+10 %), then write the same config again and read the result.
Config bits NOP[1:0] must be 01 or the write is ignored. Single-ended AIN0 at +/-4.096 V, 128 SPS = 0xC38B; temperature mode = 0x859B.
Inputs must stay between GND and VIN (+/-0.3 V) whatever full-scale range is chosen; at 3.3 V the +/-4.096 V range reads 0-3.3 V.
The board has two 6-pin headers on opposite edges; both GND pins and both VIN pins are joined on the board.

driver.code:
# ADS1118 16-bit SPI ADC with internal temperature sensor (Texas Instruments SBAS457F), MicroPython driver.
# SPI mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1), SCLK up to 4 MHz (tSCLK >= 250 ns).
# Every 16-bit transfer clocks the 16-bit Config register in on DIN while the last conversion
# result is clocked out on DOUT (Figure 42). Single-shot use, as in the datasheet:
#   1. write the Config word with SS = 1 -> starts one conversion (device is in power-down)
#   2. wait one conversion period (1 / data rate, +10 % oscillator tolerance)
#   3. write the same Config word again and read the 16-bit result in the same transfer
# Config word (Table 7): SS | MUX[2:0] | PGA[2:0] | MODE | DR[2:0] | TS_MODE | PULL_UP_EN | NOP[1:0]=01 | 1
# ADC result: 16-bit two's complement, LSB = FSR / 2^15 (Table 3; 125 uV at +/-4.096 V).
# Temperature: 14-bit two's complement, left-justified, 0.03125 degC per LSB (Table 4).
from machine import Pin
import time

_FSR = {6.144: 0, 4.096: 1, 2.048: 2, 1.024: 3, 0.512: 4, 0.256: 5}
_DR = {8: 0, 16: 1, 32: 2, 64: 3, 128: 4, 250: 5, 475: 6, 860: 7}


class ADS1118:
    def __init__(self, spi, cs, fsr=4.096, data_rate=128):
        """spi: machine.SPI with polarity=0, phase=1 (SPI mode 1), <= 4 MHz.
        cs: GPIO number of CS. fsr: full-scale range in volts (6.144, 4.096, 2.048,
        1.024, 0.512 or 0.256). Inputs must still stay between GND and VDD."""
        if fsr not in _FSR:
            raise ValueError('fsr must be one of 6.144, 4.096, 2.048, 1.024, 0.512, 0.256')
        if data_rate not in _DR:
            raise ValueError('data_rate must be 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 250, 475 or 860')
        self.spi = spi
        self.cs = Pin(cs, Pin.OUT, value=1)
        self.fsr = fsr
        self._pga = _FSR[fsr]
        self._dr = _DR[data_rate]
        self._wait_ms = 1100 // data_rate + 2  # one conversion, +10 % data-rate tolerance
        self._tx = bytearray(2)
        self._rx = bytearray(2)

    def _xfer(self, cfg):
        self._tx[0] = cfg >> 8
        self._tx[1] = cfg & 0xFF
        self.cs.value(0)
        self.spi.write_readinto(self._tx, self._rx)
        self.cs.value(1)  # CS high resets the serial interface (16-bit cycle)
        return (self._rx[0] << 8) | self._rx[1]

    def _convert(self, cfg):
        self._xfer(cfg)               # SS = 1: start a single-shot conversion
        time.sleep_ms(self._wait_ms)  # wait for it to finish
        return self._xfer(cfg)        # read the result (same config written again)

    def _cfg(self, mux, ts):
        # SS=1, MUX, PGA, MODE=1 (single-shot), DR, TS_MODE, PULL_UP_EN=1, NOP=01, reserved=1
        return (0x8000 | (mux << 12) | (self._pga << 9) | 0x0100 |
                (self._dr << 5) | (0x10 if ts else 0) | 0x08 | 0x02 | 0x01)

    def read_raw(self, channel):
        """Single-ended reading of AIN<channel> against GND (MUX 100..111); signed 16-bit code."""
        if not 0 <= channel <= 3:
            raise ValueError('ADS1118 channel must be 0-3')
        raw = self._convert(self._cfg(4 + channel, False))
        return raw - 0x10000 if raw & 0x8000 else raw

    def raw_to_volts(self, raw):
        return raw * self.fsr / 32768

    def read_volts(self, channel):
        return self.raw_to_volts(self.read_raw(channel))

    def temperature(self):
        """Internal temperature sensor in degC (TS_MODE = 1). MUX/PGA keep their reset values."""
        raw = self._convert(0x8000 | (0 << 12) | (2 << 9) | 0x0100 | (self._dr << 5) | 0x10 | 0x08 | 0x02 | 0x01) >> 2
        if raw & 0x2000:
            raw -= 0x4000
        return raw * 0.03125

example.code:
from machine import Pin, SPI
import time
from ads1118 import ADS1118

# SPI mode 1 (polarity=0, phase=1) as the ADS1118 datasheet requires
spi = SPI(1, baudrate=1000000, polarity=0, phase=1, sck=Pin({SCK}), mosi=Pin({DIN}), miso=Pin({OUT}))
adc = ADS1118(spi, {CS}, fsr=4.096)  # +/-4.096 V range: 125 uV per count
while True:
    raw = adc.read_raw(0)
    t = adc.temperature()
    print('A0 raw=%d V=%.4f T=%.2fC' % (raw, adc.raw_to_volts(raw), t))
    time.sleep(1)
